content.comment_body: I am creating an RPM display using [article_no], and noticed that a function within the mathematical tool lets you reference other program sections for data multiplication. With [article_no] the reference option is missing from the mathematical function. Any idea why this feature was removed?

Just below the mathematical block, you'll find a small icon with a plus sign. Click on it and you can create reference connections in the same way as standard electrical ones. When finished, click the minus symbol under the block and the reference lines will disappear, yet still exist in the program. There's a symbol on the workspace to show or hide these reference lines. P.S. I spent some time figuring this out. Apologies for my English.
That solution works, thanks. Your English was fine.
I’m not sure who came up with this design—it's straightforward once you know how, but I spent an hour trying to figure it out. Thanks!

analysis.insight_summary: Users had trouble finding the mathematical reference tool in the newer revision of [product_name] programming software, as its location and workflow changed compared to the prior version. This resulted in frustration and time spent searching before discovering the redesigned feature. Once its usage was clarified, users found it simple, though initially unintuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the reference tool for mathematical functions to be easily accessible and immediately obvious in new versions, without requiring extra effort or consulting outside documentation.
